[THOUGHT] The clinical impression is highly consistent with classic erythema infectiosum: biphasic rash (slapped-cheek → lacy reticular), appropriate viral prodrome, absence of systemic toxicity, and age- and presentation-typical features. While Parvovirus B19 IgM is pending, the diagnosis of acute parvovirus B19 infection is *clinically definitive* in this setting — serology is confirmatory but not required for diagnosis when the classic triad (facial erythema + reticular rash + mild prodrome) is present. No red flags are present (e.g., pallor, fatigue, tachycardia, or lab evidence of anemia suggesting aplastic crisis; no arthralgias pointing to persistent infection; no pregnancy or immunocompromise raising concern for complications). The case summary provides sufficient clinical detail to support the diagnosis without ambiguity. Turn limit is 5/10, so there is capacity to wait for IgM — but it is not *necessary* to do so for diagnostic sufficiency.

[DECISION] PASS
